en.askTitle: Put in your own city, budget and programmes and get the same full-year cost check and shortfall for each course
en.runTitle: A French graduate’s one-year UK master’s from September 2027: is EUR 44,000 enough?

fields.label: Total budget in EUR, and how much is family money
fields.value: EUR 44,000 in total, of which EUR 38,000 is family money

fields.label: Programmes, universities and tuition fees in GBP
fields.value: a one-year taught master’s in data analytics or international business, in London and Manchester

en.template: Help me plan a one-year master's in the UK from {start} while living in {city}. I have {budget} and I am looking at {programmes}. Rebuild the full-year budget with the Student visa fee, the Immigration Health Surcharge, living costs for {city} and the current exchange rate, show the shortfall for each programme and the tuition that would fit my budget, and list the scholarships I may be eligible for, marking anything unconfirmed. Ask before contacting anyone or paying anything.

phases.title: Read the official visa, fee, scholarship, rent and exchange-rate pages
phases.note: Student visa and Graduate route rules, university fee pages, scholarship lists, rents and the euro–pound rate
phases.judgment: It did not take a scholarship’s name as proof of eligibility. The British Council’s scholarships do cover French students, but only the 2026-27 list was confirmed, so the 2027-28 list is marked unconfirmed. Commonwealth, Marshall and Manchester’s two country-restricted awards were ruled out for France.

phases.title: Write the go / no-go guide with the full-year budget and sources
phases.judgment: Where it could not find a rule, it said so. The health surcharge assumes a 16-month visa, giving £1,164, and that is marked unconfirmed, because on a visa of 12 months or less it would be £776.

phases.title: Two independent checks, with fixes in between, then a phone and desktop layout test
phases.judgment: A separate colleague recomputed every money figure on their own and found only a €1 rounding slip, plus five wording or sourcing fixes. After the page was edited a second colleague re-checked each fix and the figures, and passed it, with three small wording items left open.

workers: Read the universities’ own fee pages for one-year master’s courses in London and Manchester, and what they say about EU students paying international fees
Collected student-hall prices, dated room and studio rent examples in London and Manchester, official rent statistics, university living-cost estimates and the euro–pound rate
Checked which scholarships a French student can actually apply for: Chevening, Commonwealth, Marshall, British Council, Erasmus+ and university awards
Independent check: recomputed every money figure on their own and traced the guide’s claims back to the sources list
Second check after the guide was edited: confirmed each of the five fixes and re-ran every figure
